docRequirement: `admin-setup.md:91` is the "Customization lockdown" row of the § Managed settings control table. The key is spelled `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` and it must "Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings". The canonical spec the row links (`settings.md:328` and `settings.md:1169`-`:1191`) binds the value shape and the per-surface behaviour: managed settings only; `true` locks all four surfaces and an array locks only the named ones out of exactly `skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, `mcp`. A locked `skills` blocks `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` while plugin skills, bundled skills and skills in the managed policy directory still load; a locked `agents` blocks `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` while plugin, built-in and managed-directory agents still load; a locked `hooks` blocks hooks in user, project and local `settings.json` while plugin hooks and hooks in managed settings still load; a locked `mcp` blocks servers in `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json` while plugin MCP servers and `managed-mcp.json` servers still load. One parse rule is stated explicitly: "Surface names that a Claude Code version doesn't recognize are ignored rather than failing the settings file."
current:
The key has NO first-party reader. `ManagedPiPolicyV1` does not declare it, and `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534) is 32 entries that do not include it, so `refuseUnknownKeys` (managed-policy.ts:727-733) records `sink.drop(key, 'invalid managed Pi policy key: strictPluginOnlyCustomization', 'stripped')` and the admin document loses the key before any enforcement site is reached. `grep -ran` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` returns nothing; the only five hits in the tree are gitignored build output (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js plus the four copies under apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js), one vendored Claude zod field each, declared and never read.

Per surface, what we do have:

- `hooks` — EQUIVALENT BEHAVIOUR UNDER A DIFFERENT KEY. `allowManagedHooksOnly` (managed-policy.ts:177, parsed at :1329-1332 with an invalid value read at the ENFORCING pole, exposed by `isManagedHooksOnly` :1597-1600) is resolved into `managedHookLock` at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11284-11287 and enforced in `buildPinnedAgentAutomationSystem` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-automations.ts:94-106, :118-119, :144) where every native and project hook config is skipped whole (`if (managedHooksOnly) continue`) and plugin hooks survive only when their plugin is managed force-enabled. `disableAllHooks` (managed-policy.ts:191) is the harder switch beside it.
- `mcp` — NARROWER, and keyed on NAME/IDENTITY rather than origin. `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (managed-policy.ts:508-509, parsed :1307-1313) are applied to native inventory records at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:704-713, and only on Pi turns because `if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true` at :699 returns first. There is no "plugin and managed only" pole: `allowedMcpServers: []` blocks plugin servers too (storage-runtime.ts:732-733). Already filed as not implemented at docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95.
- `skills` and `agents` — NOTHING. `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:880-1136) discovers both from user-controlled tiers and no managed key touches any of them: global `~/.agents/skills`, `<CONFIG_DIR>/skills` and `<CONFIG_DIR>/agents` (native-sources.ts:903-905), workspace `<workspaceRoot>/skills` and `<workspaceRoot>/*.md` agents (:949-950), trusted-project `<project>/.nessy-agent/skills` and `<project>/.nessy-agent/agents` (:1016-1017), and the nested portable `.agents/skills` ancestor layers (:1063-1066). `CONFIG_DIR` is the USER's config dir `~/.nessy-agent` (packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:18-21), and `getManagedSkillsRoot()` (packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:27-29) returns `<CONFIG_DIR>/skills` — the bundled-seed root, not an admin tier. The one filter over that inventory (storage-runtime.ts:692-715) drops seeded bundled skills, connector-origin sources and managed-denied MCP records, and passes every skill and agent record through untouched. Our admin channel also carries no components to substitute: managed settings are one `managed-policy.json` plus a `managed-policy.d/` drop-in directory (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52, :62-67), never scanned for skills or agents — the same emptiness recorded for hooks at packages/shared/src/config/managed-approval.ts:16-18.
- A SECOND, policy-free skills reader exists and bypasses the capability snapshot entirely. `loadAllSkills` (packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:461-494) merges global + workspace + (trusted) project tiers and is called with no policy in sight from packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:825 (→ `onSkillsListChange` → `broadcastSkillsChanged`, SessionManager.ts:7016-7023 and :7440 — the renderer's Skills list), SessionManager.ts:973 (Skill-tool display metadata) and SessionManager.ts:18650 (`resolveAutomationMentions`, which turns an `@slug` into a `skillSlugs` entry on a real send).
divergence:
Three deltas, one of them cosmetic and two not.

(1) THE KEY NAME IS ABSENT, not merely unenforced. `refuseUnknownKeys` (managed-policy.ts:727-733) strips the documented spelling — no alias, no partial parse — so even the one surface we genuinely enforce is unreachable through the documented key. An administrator pasting a working Claude Code managed-settings block gets a policy that reads as deployed and locks nothing.

(2) `hooks` HAS THE RIGHT BEHAVIOUR UNDER THE WRONG KEY. `allowManagedHooksOnly` already produces exactly the doc's hooks row (user/project/local hook tiers dropped whole, force-enabled plugin hooks kept). For that quarter this is a key-name-only divergence: mapping `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: ['hooks']` onto the existing `managedHookLock.enabled` is a one-line OR at SessionManager.ts:11284.

(3) `skills` AND `agents` HAVE NO MECHANISM AT ALL — no key, no predicate, no filter. `allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins` narrow WHICH PLUGINS load and never touch a native record; `availableModels` restricts which model a skill may use, never where the skill came from. The only gate on the project tier is `projectTrustState === 'trusted'` (native-sources.ts:995) / `projectTrusted` (skills/storage.ts:484), i.e. the per-user project-trust prompt — a USER decision, which is precisely the decision this admin key exists to take away.

One parse rule diverges in advance: the page requires an unrecognised SURFACE NAME to be ignored while the rest of the key still applies, whereas the generic list parser `list()` (managed-policy.ts:783-797) throws on any invalid entry and fails the whole field. The new key must therefore not be routed through `list()`/`grant`/`restrict`.

And `mcp` is narrower rather than absent: a denylist by name, URL or argv is not an origin lock, and it lapses entirely on non-Pi turns (storage-runtime.ts:699).

change.what: Add `export type StrictCustomizationSurfaceV1 = 'skills' | 'agents' | 'hooks' | 'mcp'` plus a `STRICT_CUSTOMIZATION_SURFACES` constant, and `readonly strictPluginOnlyCustomization?: readonly StrictCustomizationSurfaceV1[]` on `ManagedPiPolicyV1` beside the other admin locks (:177-:203). NORMALIZE at parse time — `true` becomes the full four-element array — so no reader ever sees the `true | array` union (carrying that union past the parser is the 'read at one call site and forgotten at the next' failure the :1593-:1596 comment names). Add `'strictPluginOnlyCustomization'` to `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (:501-534, today 32 entries). Parse it beside `allowManagedHooksOnly` (:1329-1332): `true` → all four; an array → FILTER to known surface names and keep the valid subset with NO drop recorded (settings.md:1191 — unknown surface names are ignored, not fatal), which is why it must NOT go through `list()` (:783-797); `false` → undefined; any other value → read at the ENFORCING pole (all four) with disposition `tightened`, the same admin-lock polarity as :1325-1332. Emit it in the frozen return (:1440-1475). Add `export function isStrictPluginOnlyCustomizationLocked(policy: ManagedPiPolicyV1, surface: StrictCustomizationSurfaceV1): boolean` next to `isManagedHooksOnly` (:1597-1600). Leave `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_WIDENING_KEYS` (:555-563) alone — the key only ever narrows, so `isManagedPolicyTightening` already classifies adding it as a tightening. `carriesManagedSettings` (:1155-1160) is generic over keys and needs no edit.

This is the single choke point where native skill AND agent records meet `managedPiPolicy`. Under a `skills` lock drop `record.kind === 'skill'`, under an `agents` lock drop `record.kind === 'agent'`, for `record.scope.kind` in `global | workspace | project` — all three are user-controlled here, since `<CONFIG_DIR>` is the user's own dir. Bundled skills must SURVIVE the `skills` lock (settings.md:1187 'Still loads: … bundled skills'): reuse the existing seeded-bundled-skill pair check — `seededSkillsRoot` (:662) and `bundledSkillSlugs` (:678-686) — inverted, i.e. exempt a skill whose `dirname(record.sourcePath)` is a seeded bundled path. Put the new checks BEFORE the `if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true` early return at :699: that gate is exactly why the managed MCP filter does not cover non-Pi turns, and an origin lock that silently lapses on a Claude or Codex turn is the 'declared on one path, enforced on another' defect this file keeps guarding against. If the `mcp` surface is implemented too, apply it beside the identity checks at :704-713 (both `record.kind === 'mcp'` and `record.sourceType === 'mcp'`).

Three edits. (a) One line at :11284: `enabled: isManagedHooksOnly(this.managedPiPolicy) || isStrictPluginOnlyCustomizationLocked(this.managedPiPolicy, 'hooks')`, adding the predicate to the import at :36; `pluginHooksVetted` stays as-is because the doc's hooks row keeps plugin hooks and the force-enabled carve-out already expresses that. Nothing changes inside runtime-automations.ts. (b) `broadcastSkillsChanged` and (c) `resolveAutomationMentions` are fed by `loadAllSkills`, which never sees a policy: filter their `LoadedSkill[]` by `skill.source` ('global' | 'workspace' | 'project' dropped, plugin kept) when the `skills` surface is locked. Doing it here rather than inside `loadAllSkills` keeps `shared`'s watcher free of managed policy, which it has no access to.

Recommended, not strictly required: widen `scope` to `'global' | 'workspace' | 'project'` and `reason` to `'untrusted-project' | 'managed-plugin-only-customization'` so a locked surface produces the same safe, path-free diagnostic the untrusted-project case already does (native-sources.ts:1119-1124). Without it a user sees skills and agents silently vanish with no explanation. Note the producer of `blockedLayers` is native-sources, which takes no policy, so the new layer has to be appended where the filter runs (storage-runtime.ts, on the `nativeInventory` assembled at :722-725).

blastRadius:
Crosses a PERSISTENCE and a WIRE boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. `ManagedPiPolicyV1` is not a local type: the same document arrives from a host-owned file plus `managed-policy.d/` fragments (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-67) AND from a server-delivered payload that is salvaged and cached at mode 0600 (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts), is composed by `composeManagedPolicySources` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:191-212) and resolved by `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-139). Composition needs no per-key counterpart — the winner is taken wholesale, only `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` and `sandbox.network` are special-cased — but the reachability property pinned at storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts:160/:183 fails by construction until the field round-trips. `isManagedPolicyTightening` (managed-policy.ts:604-640) decides whether a mid-session re-read applies now or at a turn boundary, and `managedPolicyEquals`/`canonicalPolicyJson` (:588-602) hash the whole key set.

On the enforcement side the filter feeds `EffectiveCapabilitySnapshot`, which projects three ways (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:1-12): `toAgentRuntime` for the agent and `toComposerCatalog`/`toUserCatalog` for the renderer. Locked skills and agents therefore disappear from the Skills and Agents lists as well as from the turn — intended, but a visible product change. The Pi harness manifest hashes both (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts), so a locked fleet gets a different manifest generation.

Three boundaries the change must not assume it covers. (a) The `loadAllSkills` bypass: packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:825, SessionManager.ts:973, :7016-7023 and :18650 read skills without any policy, so a lock enforced only in the capability filter still leaks into the renderer Skills list and into automation `@mention` resolution. (b) The workspace MCP browse pool is provider-neutral by contract (docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md § 'The provider guard'), so an `mcp` surface enforced only in the capability inputs still lets the Sources UI connect a blocked server. (c) Imported plugin paths must be left alone: the Claude and Codex format adapters keep contributing skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from PLUGIN bundles, which is exactly what every locked surface must continue to load.
userImpact:
For an administrator, today: deploying the documented key in `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, in a `managed-policy.d/` fragment, or through the server-delivered payload does nothing whatsoever. It is stripped as an unknown key, so `nessy-general-agent doctor` prints `invalid managed Pi policy key: strictPluginOnlyCustomization` with disposition `stripped` — the failure is visible rather than silent, but the fleet stays unlocked on three of the four surfaces the admin-setup control table promises. The one that works has to be reached by a different name (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), which the admin has no way to learn from Claude's docs.

For an end user on such a fleet: every skill in `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.nessy-agent/skills`, `<workspace>/skills` and a trusted project's `.nessy-agent/skills`, and every subagent in `~/.nessy-agent/agents`, `<workspace>/*.md` and `<project>/.nessy-agent/agents`, still appears in the Skills and Agents lists, is still offered to the model, is still `@`-mentionable in an automation, and is still invocable — including one a repository shipped, as soon as the project-trust dialog is accepted. That per-user trust prompt is the only gate, and it is the user's call, not the administrator's.
